name: attention_distribution_wealth_politics_comments
description: Who receives attention: (1) wealthy versus poor people at the perceptual, media and political level and how this changed over time; (2) attention captured on social media by right-wing parties (AfD) and by state actors of Russia and China; (3) studies analysing user comments on zeit.de. All measured values are untagged (default); conjectures from the dialogue carry the tag 'assumed' with a confidence number 0 to 1. Sources without a verified DOI are marked doi_verified false. Original requests (German): 'gibt es Studien, wie viel mehr Aufmerksamkeit wohlhabenden Menschen im Vergleich zu aermeren zu Teil wird und wie sich dies ueber die Zeit veraendert hat?'; 'Wurde schon mal gemessen, wie viel Aufmerksamkeit sich rechte Gruppen (MAGA, AfD, ...) und intolerante Regimes wie das in Russland und China ueber die sozialen Medien klauen?'; 'Gibt es Studien, die die Nutzerkommentare auf zeit.de analysieren?'; 'Alle Studien mit moeglichst vielen Zahlen gerne als json.'

words.name: rich-poor attention ratio over time is unquantified
words.description: claim: no study measures a single ratio of attention to the rich versus the poor as a time series.

words.name: wealthy receive more attention and give less
words.description: claim: high status attracts gaze (Dalmaso) while higher-class individuals look less at others (Dietze), an asymmetry in social attention.

words.name: economic news bias is stable over three decades
words.description: claim: the tracking of the rich by economic news tone (Jacobs 2021) is the most robust long-run time series available.

words.name: Swiss rich list press replication is feasible
words.description: claim: Ischinsky's design (rich list plus press corpus) can be reproduced for Switzerland.

words.name: AfD advantage stems from community strategy rather than algorithm alone
words.description: claim: unofficial supporter networks and early platform presence explain much of the AfD reach; algorithm as sole cause is contested (Bertelsmann Potsdam audit).

words.name: attention flows to conflict not only to the right
words.description: claim: anti-AfD content also gained views in 2025, so outrage about the right feeds attention to it.

words.name: foreign state operations capture a small share of feed attention
words.description: claim: directly stolen attention by Russian and Chinese operations is tiny relative to domestic media and politicians (Eady 2023) and inflated by fake engagement (Schliebs 2021).

words.name: foreign influence works mainly through domestic amplifiers
words.description: claim: the effect of state operations runs indirectly via domestic actors picking up narratives.

words.name: no dedicated zeit.de comment corpus study exists
words.description: claim: apart from Taddicken 2010, zeit.de appears only as one site among many in multi-site studies; no released corpus comparable to One Million Posts.

words.name: moderated comment corpora miss deleted comments
words.description: claim: any zeit.de comment corpus systematically lacks the deleted, most severe comments.
